cells.tense: Right now, in the shared thing you're part of, you're the one turning it.
cells.act: finish the thing that has been waiting on its last step
cells.ask: Pick a shared practice that's run its course and do its final piece with the people it held, then stop. Don't name a successor.
cells.core:
What's arriving in the shared thing you're part of, you meet as it comes. Not bracing for what it will turn into, not holding the old form a season past its season. You can tell when a practice has run its course, and you finish it without the next one already designed.

The growth here is finishing without sealing shut. A cycle ending isn't a loss that needs a fast replacement; the space after it stays open until something real shows up. So do one ending plainly — tell the people it held that it's done, and fill the space that follows with nothing. What stays unfilled tends itself. An ending that makes room, not a wall.
cells.sheetLine: What's ending here can close and stay open.
cells.place: where a shared thing is carried forward

cells.tense: You'll be somewhere ahead of the shared thing, managing how it'll look before it's even started.
cells.act: complete it without making it final
cells.ask: Attend one shared thing through its plain middle — the unexciting meeting, the ordinary version — and don't improve, end, or swap it out that week.
cells.core:
You're already living in how the shared thing turns out. The group's ritual, how people gather — you can see three moves ahead, and you're steering toward a version that hasn't arrived. From where you stand that's foresight. Everyone else sits through a thing still forming while you've already filed it.

The corrective is not restraint; it's contact. Sit inside one shared thing while it's still routine and alive, alongside the people it holds, and keep it unfinished on purpose. Notice what it's carrying for someone who isn't you. The endings you make after that will be fewer and better timed. You don't have to end a thing to be free of it.
cells.sheetLine: You're managing the ending before the thing has started.
cells.place: where a shared thing is carried forward

cells.tense: You were part of something shared that ended, and you're still standing at its door.
cells.act: gather what it became and set it down whole
cells.ask: Gather what a shared thing actually gave the people in it, set that down whole once, and clear its standing slot from your calendar.
cells.core:
A shared thing ended and you kept its slot on the calendar. The practice still meets, the familiar lines still get spoken, and the thing itself stopped. You're not inside it and you're not free of it. The time it takes is time a living practice could use, and the gap between keeping and living shows in whoever is still showing up.

Gather what it became — what it actually gave the people in it — and set that down whole, once, where you can see it. Then the slot is empty and yours. Nothing has to be announced as over; a finished thing stops asking for you. What fills the space next is a separate question, and it can wait until the space is actually clear.
cells.sheetLine: It ended. You're still keeping the door open.
cells.place: where a shared thing is carried forward

cells.tense: You're in a shared thing that's changing shape, and you'd say it's just how things go.
cells.act: choose this, not that, and mean it
cells.ask: Take a shared thing you keep attending out of habit, decide once whether you're actually in it, and answer the next invitation from that decision rather than the groove.
cells.core:
Something in what you share is shifting — how people gather, the account the group gives of itself — and the person steering it is you. Ask and you'd say it just evolved. The change has an author; the author isn't signing. So the results keep arriving as surprises, and the same shape keeps coming back around because nobody chose it away.

Aim your attention at one shared thing and decide: this, not that, and mean it. Not forever — for now. The next time it's expected of you, answer from the decision rather than the groove. That's the whole act. A direction you picked from what's here is different from one you inherited, even when it looks identical from outside. You get to know which one you're in.
cells.sheetLine: The change in this has an author. It's you.
cells.place: where a shared thing is carried forward
